info.bio:
Roger Keith ("Syd") Barrett (* Cambridge, Inglaterra, 6 de enero de 1946 - † Cambridge, Inglaterra, 7 de julio de 2006), conocido como Syd Barrett, fue uno de los fundadores del grupo de rock psicodélico Pink Floyd.
Fue el líder como cantante, guitarrista y compositor de la banda en su primer y exitoso album The Piper at the Gates of Dawn (1967). A medida que la fama de Pink Floyd crecía, su abuso de drogas psicoactivas (especialmente LSD) fue afectándole cada vez más

scenes.name: El underground de Londres
scenes.author: Jon Savage
scenes.desc: En Gran Bretaña el LSD circulaba por el mismo tipo de gente que en Estados Unidos: estudiantes de arte, hipsters, bohemios y poetas, muchos llegados desde la CND. Su primera gran reunión fue la International Poetry Incarnation del Albert Hall (junio de 1965: Ginsberg, Trocchi, Burroughs, Adrian Mitchell), filmada por Peter Whitehead. En enero de 1966 John Hopkins y Steve Stollman montaron en el Marquee el primer Spontaneous Underground, intento, como los Acid Tests, de crear un entorno que se acercara a la disrupción perceptiva del LSD; el 13 de marzo, «The Trip», con el grupo de improvisación AMM y el debut en el Marquee de unos Pink Floyd que dejaban las versiones de R&B. En febrero Barry Miles y John Dunbar abrieron la librería Indica (ESP-Disk, Burroughs, Leary, Artaud, Crowley, Gurdjieff, Blavatsky), con la ayuda de Paul McCartney. En abril Miles y Hopkins repartieron en la marcha de la CND THE Global moon-edition Long Hair TIMES.

scenes.name: Alicia, la locura y el regreso a la infancia
scenes.author: Jon Savage
scenes.desc: Al final de 1966 el LSD llevó al pop de vuelta a la infancia y a la locura. Los Beatles empezaron el 24 de noviembre «Strawberry Fields Forever», un viaje de Lennon hacia abajo, no hacia atrás, al orfanato junto a su casa, «psicoanálisis con música», unida por Geoff Emerick a partir de dos tomas; luego «When I’m Sixty-Four» y «Penny Lane». En Navidad la BBC aplazó el Alice in Wonderland de Jonathan Miller, sin cabezas de animal, con el sitar de Ravi Shankar y rodado en un hospital militar de víctimas de neurosis de guerra: un catálogo de psicosis. Grace Slick llevó «White Rabbit» a Jefferson Airplane; Syd Barrett escribía sobre el mundo de Lewis Carroll. Proliferaban los discos sobre la locura («They’re Coming to Take Me Away, Ha-Haaa!», «Pandora’s Golden Heebie Jeebies» de los Association), y en el corazón secreto del año, la tristeza frágil de «How Can We Hang On to a Dream» de Tim Hardin.

scenes.name: Psicodelia y underground postpsicodélico
scenes.book: Postpunk. Romper todo y empezar de nuevo
scenes.author: Simon Reynolds
scenes.desc: La música industrial es «el segundo florecimiento de una auténtica psicodelia», pero invertida: comparte con los happenings y los acid tests la sobrecarga sensorial multimedia y el imperativo de que «ningún sonido quede sin procesar». Genesis P-Orridge venía del underground (The Fugs, Pearls Before Swine, el Exploding Galaxy); COUM telonea a Hawkwind en 1971; Chris Carter se convierte viendo a Pink Floyd bajo los efectos del ácido y diseña luces para Yes y Hawkwind.

scenes.name: Locura psicodélica y space-rock
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: El boom psicodélico y el desacondicionamiento hippy alumbran una generación de originales: Syd Barrett y sus dos obras maestras de folk psicodélico (Madcap Laughs, Barrett), Twink y los Pink Fairies, Peter Green (The End Of The Game), Hawkwind, inventores del space-rock entre la cultura hippy y el punk. En EE UU, Bruce Palmer, David Crosby (If I Could Only Remember My Name), Merrell Fankhauser y Mu, Ya Ho Wha 13. En Japón nace el space-rock con Hadaka no Rallizes, la Taj Mahal Travellers («La Monte Young con ácido»), Keiji Haino y Fushitsusha.

podcast.title: Summer 1967 - Point of No Return
podcast.body: A pivotal weekend in the summer of 1967, when Sid Baret went on a five-day excursion with friends involving drugs, is identified as his point of no return. After this event, his sister noted he no longer recognized some people, couldn't remember lyrics, and often fell into catatonic states, remaining motionless for 8-10 hours without blinking. This is believed to be due to severe LSD abuse, marking a permanent change in him. "En ese momento Sid Baret ya cambia para siempre."

srcs.episode: Pink Floyd: Tras los pasos de Syd Barrett

podcast.title: Dramatic Appearance During "Wish You Were Here" Recordings (1975)
podcast.body: In 1975, while Pin Floyd was in the studio completing "Wish You Were Here," Sid Baret unexpectedly appeared, completely shaven, pale, without eyelashes or eyebrows, and in a "horrible state." This moment, captured in two or three historical photos, deeply impacted Roger Waters, who broke down crying upon seeing his childhood friend. This event profoundly changed the lives of the band members and the band's history. "Aparece completamente rapado, muy pálido, sin pestañas, sin cejas, en un estado horrible y según nos cuenta un ayudante ingeniero de sonido que estaba allí, Roger Waters rompía llorar totalmente desgarrado por el estado en el que estaba Sid Baret."

srcs.episode: Pink Floyd: Tras los pasos de Syd Barrett

podcast.title: Financial Struggles and Pin Floyd's Support (1978)
podcast.body: By 1978, Sid Baret, despite having earned substantial money from Pin Floyd and ongoing royalties from their first two albums, ran out of money while living in London. He moved back to Cambridge to live with his family. Pin Floyd made several gestures, including re-editions and securing rights, to ensure he continued to receive royalties as a full member (even for works where he contributed minimally, like the second album). This financial support allowed him and his family to live comfortably without money worries for the rest of his life. "La banda tenía un último gesto hacia el artista para ayudar a generar un poco más de dinero y que pudiese acabar en paz y sin problemas económicos al resto de sus días."

srcs.episode: Pink Floyd: Tras los pasos de Syd Barrett

podcast.title: "Lonely Genius" Archetype
podcast.body: Syd Barrett is frequently portrayed as a "lonely genius" whose creativity seemed to flourish in the isolation of the recording studio. His personal struggles and mental health issues are presented as part of a recurring pattern among artists facing intense pressure to innovate and exceed expectations. "Sid Barrett de Pink Floyd... han sido frecuentemente retratados como genio solitarios, cuya creatividad parece florecer en la soledad del estudio de grabación."

srcs.episode: El Álbum Perdido que pudo cambiar la música ｜ Smile de The Beach Boys

podcast.title: Catatonic States and Disappearances
podcast.body: Even during Pin Floyd's rapid ascent and the recording of their first album in 1967, Sid Baret frequently entered catatonic states. He also had episodes where he literally disappeared for weeks, highlighting the early signs of his deteriorating condition. "un Sid Baret que a veces se entraba en verdadero estado catatónico y en conciertos de 1967 incluso en la agravación del primer álbum."

srcs.episode: Pink Floyd: Tras los pasos de Syd Barrett

podcast.title: Challenges in Solo Recording
podcast.body: Recording Sid Baret's solo material was extremely difficult due to his mental state. Collaborating musicians from Sob Machine and other bands were reportedly obligated rather than voluntary participants. Roger Waters and David Gilmore, who produced his solo work, found it "very complicated." The sound engineer deemed it "absolutely unbearable, impossible," as Sid Baret would play erratically, sometimes brilliantly, sometimes just banging or breaking his guitar, and could not remember what he had played. "decía que llora absolutamente insoportable imposible."

srcs.episode: Pink Floyd: Tras los pasos de Syd Barrett

podcast.title: Comparison to John Frusciante's Early Solo Work
podcast.body: Syd Barrett is used as a point of comparison for John Frusciante's early solo album, "Niandra LaDes and Usually Just a T-Shirt." The comparison stems from similarities in the unpolished nature of the ideas, low recording quality, strange and critical lyrics, and the shared history of severe drug abuse and eccentric behavior. However, it is noted that Barrett's issues were rooted in real mental health problems that plagued him his entire life, while Frusciante's similar behaviors were largely attributed to drug use. "se empieza a hacer ciertas comparaciones con Sidbare al mejor salvando mucho las distancias."

srcs.episode: La historia de John Frusciante: Talento, creatividad y guitarras.

podcast.title: Comprehensive Biography
podcast.body: An extensive biography, considered one of the most interesting books on music, provides a very human vision of Sid Baret's time in Pin Floyd. It includes narratives from Roger Waters, David Gilmore, and crucially, his sister, who was his closest relative. This biography offers a less sensationalist perspective on his departure from Pin Floyd, presenting a nuanced view that helps understand the early years of the band. "nos da una visión como muy humana de esa parte, una visión como muy personal que además no solo está contada con Roger Waters."

srcs.episode: Pink Floyd: Tras los pasos de Syd Barrett

podcast.title: Compulsive Pursuit of Pin Floyd
podcast.body: After his expulsion, Sid Baret exhibited compulsive behavior, pursuing Pin Floyd by appearing at their concerts and recording sessions. He would show up at EMI studios, attempting to enter through fire exits, even after knowing he was no longer a member. In one instance, he chased the band to Ibiza, appearing at the airport in a frantic state. These episodes were tragic, as he remained friends with Roger Waters and David Gilmore. "Sid Baret acabó haciendo un comportamiento durante años compulsivo persiguiendo a Pin Floyd en conciertos y van la estudio de grabación."

srcs.episode: Pink Floyd: Tras los pasos de Syd Barrett

podcast.title: Disappearance and Psychiatric Internment
podcast.body: During his solo recording period, Sid Baret once disappeared for several months, driving his Mini around the United Kingdom in a sudden fit. He was later found interned in a psychiatric hospital, having been admitted after causing a scandal in a lamentable state, without anyone knowing he was Sid Baret. The band had to rescue him from the institution. "varios meses más tarde se lo encontraron en un entrenado, un psiquiátrico que alguien no había cogido, un estado lamentable montándome escándalo y la habían acabado internando sin saber que era Sid Baret."

srcs.episode: Pink Floyd: Tras los pasos de Syd Barrett

podcast.title: Distorted and Eccentric Guitar
podcast.body: Syd Barrett was known for his highly distorted and eccentric guitar style, a remnant of psychedelic music that later influenced glam. "esa guitarra tan distorsionada y a veces es un tanto excéntrica."

srcs.episode: EL PIONERO DEL GLAM: MARC BOLAN Y T REX

podcast.title: Eccentric Behavior and Theatricality
podcast.body: Barrett's eccentric behavior and somewhat theatrical stage presence significantly influenced Marc Bolan's evolution in 1970, particularly in shaping Bolan's image and aesthetic. "Hay mucha gente asocia mucho esa evolución que tuvo Mar Bolanc en 1970, con lo que era la imagen y la estética de Siddbarred."

srcs.episode: EL PIONERO DEL GLAM: MARC BOLAN Y T REX

podcast.title: Ejection from Pin Floyd
podcast.body: Sid Baret was eventually forced out of Pin Floyd, not due to Roger Waters' ego or jealousy among band members, but because his deteriorating mental state made his involvement unsustainable. By late 1967, his condition was lamentable, evident in concert recordings and catatonic appearances in US television interviews. His erratic and aggressive behavior, including not attending recordings, made it impossible for him to continue. "Hubo que echarlo porque no iba las grabaciones. El tenia un comportamiento estétrico."

srcs.episode: Pink Floyd: Tras los pasos de Syd Barrett

podcast.title: Erosion of Relationships with Pin Floyd Members
podcast.body: By the summer of 1971, the intense difficulties encountered during Sid Baret's solo recordings severely eroded his personal relationships with Roger Waters and David Gilmore. They became very distant and exhausted, and their relationship never fully recovered, marking a definitive end to their close bond. "la relación entre Sid Baret y Roger Waters y David Gilmore quedó muy erosionada de esta grabación, quedaron como muy tocados y un tanto distanciado durante un tiempo."

srcs.episode: Pink Floyd: Tras los pasos de Syd Barrett

podcast.title: Formation and Demise of Stars
podcast.body: In 1972, a final attempt was made to involve Sid Baret in a new group called Stars, but it lasted only a few months. Live recordings from Stars concerts are described as even "more impactful and heavy" than Pin Floyd's 1967 recordings, showcasing his severely deteriorated state. His sister ultimately advised him to abandon his musical career altogether. "De hecho, tenemos algunas grabaciones de conciertos stars que son todavía más impactantes y más heavis que esas grabaciones en 1967 que teníamos de Pin Floyd."

srcs.episode: Pink Floyd: Tras los pasos de Syd Barrett

podcast.title: Original Leader and Influence on Album Themes
podcast.body: Syd Barrett was the original leader of Pink Floyd during its early years. He was a person with very delicate emotional health, and the pressures from the record label, coupled with the band's success, ultimately led him to severe mental problems and complete reclusion at home with his family. His mental deterioration served as a significant thematic influence for Pink Floyd's album *The Dark Side of the Moon*, contributing to its exploration of madness and psychological evolution, themes that continued to resonate throughout the band's career. "el deterioro mental, que sofre o si parre, que fue el líder original de Pink Floyd al principio antes de que acabas a retirar los primeros discos."

srcs.episode: Pink Floyd - The Dark Side of The Moon (historia)

podcast.title: Reluctance of M.Y. for Solo Work
podcast.body: M.Y. Records was highly reluctant to support Sid Baret's solo career, despite recognizing his talent. They viewed him as "crazy" and, more importantly, unpredictable, making him a difficult artist to work with for recording and production. "Emmy no le gustaba nada en la idea de que Sid Baret volviese a trabajar porque a ver el vice-bale era un talento pero estaba como una cabra y sobre todo era impredecible."

srcs.episode: Pink Floyd: Tras los pasos de Syd Barrett

podcast.title: Roger Waters' Guilt
podcast.body: Roger Waters expressed significant guilt and culpability regarding Sid Baret's departure from Pin Floyd, particularly the fact that Sid Baret was already effectively out of the band before he himself was aware of it. This highlights the emotional toll of the situation on his former bandmates. "Roger Waters habla con mucha culpabilidad, con muchos sentimientos de culpabilidad porque hablaban de que llegó un punto en que Sid Baret ya estaba fuera de la banda y él no lo sabía."

srcs.episode: Pink Floyd: Tras los pasos de Syd Barrett

podcast.title: Sordid Behavior in the 1970s
podcast.body: Sid Baret's sister recounted "sordid" stories about his behavior in the 1970s, indicating a continued decline in his mental health and personal conduct during this period. "Su hermana ya en la época de 1970 nos cuenta también historias como muy sordidas del comportamiento de Sid Baret."

srcs.episode: Pink Floyd: Tras los pasos de Syd Barrett

podcast.title: The Man, The Myth, The Genius
podcast.body: Sid Baret is described as a "man myth" and the "great genius" behind the early success of Pin Floyd, yet he suffered from severe mental health issues. His exact condition remains unknown; possibilities include schizophrenia, a manic problem, Asperger's syndrome, drug abuse, or even abusive medication. His family never wished to publish his medical history, and he was never adequately medicated, leading to his continued struggles. "Sid Baret es un hombre mito, eso es así, era el gran genio que estuvo detrás del éxito de Pin Floyd pero el problema es que estaba loco."
